data.name: Silian
data.long_meaning: Silian is derived from the Latin name Silas, which was derived from the Greek name Silas. Silas was a prominent disciple of Saint Paul in the New Testament, and is considered to be one of the seventy-two disciples. Silas is also believed to have carried Paul and Barnabas' letters to various Christian communities in Greece and Asia Minor. The name Silas is derived from the Greek word silas, which means 'foreman' or 'ruler'. In the religious context, Silas represents leadership and authority in the service of the Lord.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes leadership and authority in the service of the Lord.

in_greek.name: Σιλιαν
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Σιλιαν προέρχεται από το λατινικό και σημαίνει δάσος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Σιλιαν έχει τις ρίζες του στη λατινική γλώσσα και σχετίζεται με το δάσος. Στην πρώιμη Εκκλησία, τα ονόματα που σχετίζονταν με τη φύση είχαν συχνά πνευματική σημασία. Αν και δεν υπάρχει άμεση αναφορά στο Ευαγγέλιο, το όνομα χρησιμοποιήθηκε στην παράδοση της Ανατολικής Ορθόδοξης Εκκλησίας.

historical_references.reference: Saint Silian of Perugia, also known as Silian of Assisi, was a Christian martyr who lived during the late Roman period. He was a deacon in the city of Perugia and was executed by the Romans around the year 304 due to his refusal to renounce his faith. Silian is considered a local patron saint of Perugia and his feast day is celebrated on December 8.

Saint Silian of Scythia was a Christian martyr who lived during the 3rd century. He is said to have been a bishop in Scythia, present-day Romania, and was martyred during the reign of Emperor Decius (249-251 AD). According to legend, Silian was tortured and beheaded, along with several other Christian bishops and deacons, for refusing to offer sacrifice to the Roman gods.
